title: Black Light FTL Family-Specific Route Segment Certification Registry

designIntentSource.title: The different lightspeed methods
designIntentSource.scope: Different transit methods require different gravity/miscalculation loss, safety lookahead, emergency de-transit behavior and non-perfect safety margins.

policy.routeRule: C_route = AND_i C_family,segment,i. No benign segment may average away one blocking family-specific interval.
policy.physicalRule: Physical segment envelopes remain ordinary gravity/curvature evidence. They are normalized before being passed to fictional family response.
policy.normalizationRule: Potential depth, acceleration, tidal norm and curvature scale retain their native dimensions until divided by the versioned physical normalization references.
policy.uncertaintyRule: Segment uncertainty must remain explicit. Missing covariance/1-sigma evidence produces UNRESOLVED, never zero uncertainty.
policy.familyBoundaryRule: Family-boundary hazard is fictional/operator-specific and is never inferred from ordinary gravitational metrics alone.
policy.interventionRule: Continuous-progress families may compare distance/time to the first blocking interval against the full intervention chain. PRECOMMIT families use a decision horizon instead of a fabricated local superluminal velocity.
policy.recoveryRule: Protected recovery reserve is evaluated independently of nominal drive authority and may not be spent to improve advertised route performance.
policy.invalidModelRule: OUTSIDE_MODEL_VALIDITY blocks the interval and route until a higher-fidelity physical model resolves it.

normalization.dimensionalSafeguard: Never add epsilon_Phi, |g|, ||T|| and R_* before normalization; their dimensions differ.

equations: G = w_Phi G_Phi + w_g G_g + w_T G_T + w_R G_R + w_U U_m
P_f = a_f G + b_f G^2 + c_f G^(n_f) + d_f U_m + e_f B_f
familyResponse.status: PROPOSED calibration over physically based environmental inputs
familyResponse.note: The ordinary-gravity inputs are physical. Coefficients and operator response are fictional/derived simulation models unless a higher authority establishes otherwise.

continuous: t_int = t_sensor + t_solver + t_decision + t_command + t_actuate + t_exit + t_clear + t_margin
M_D > 0 is necessary for a continuously correctable projected-progress representation.
precommit: Fold, Q-Lattice and Phase Displacement use PRECOMMIT logic unless a higher authority supplies a physically meaningful local progress representation.
intervention.safeguard: Projected progress rate is a route/control representation, not a claim that real-world local motion exceeds c.

segmentClassification.ADMISSIBLE: All physical evidence is valid and the family-specific certificate passes with positive required margins.
segmentClassification.MARGINAL: No hard gate fails, but a versioned calibration threshold identifies small remaining margin.
segmentClassification.REJECTED: A family-specific safety, observability, lookahead, recovery or efficiency condition fails.
segmentClassification.UNRESOLVED: Required evidence, calibration, family association or uncertainty is missing.
segmentClassification.OUTSIDE_MODEL_VALIDITY: The active ordinary-physics approximation is invalid for the segment.
segmentClassification.CONFLICT: Equal/higher authority inputs conflict and deterministic resolution is refused.

canonSafeguards: This registry does not claim any FTL family is physically realizable.
Physical gravity calculations constrain fictional transit response but cannot establish a race or vessel's FTL family.
Named race, vessel, manufacturer and installation sources outrank this generic registry within their documented scope.
A family selection used for simulation is not archaeological evidence of family identity.
PROPOSED coefficients, thresholds, normalization references and maturity modifiers are not constants of nature or universal setting constants.
A rejected interval remains rejected even if every other interval is admissible.
Missing uncertainty, radius, ephemeris or model validity may not be silently replaced by zero.
Emergency de-transit, shunt, closure, recoupling, detachment, return, reconciliation and braking are family-specific machinery obligations, not generic flavor text.
